name: Hyacinth Violet
lede: Hyacinth Violet is a deep, reddish purple, named for the color of the flower in its purple form.

sections.title: The flower's name
sections.body:
Paterson lists *hyacinthine* as the purplish-blue of the hyacinth, and gives hyacinth violet, or a pink, as a variant [1]. Related entries show how loose the word was: hyacinth blue is a purplish blue popular in the 1930s, and hyacinth red a reddish orange [1].

As a swatch the name is older than those entries. It appears in Ridgway's 1912 atlas on plate XI, again in the 1955 ISCC-NBS system as a deep purple, and in the 1930 Maerz and Paul dictionary [2]. Ngram data show the printed phrase peaking in the 1920s [3]. See also [[violet]], [[purple]] and [[amethyst]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Hyacinth Violet is nearly absent from painting: one painting in our archive of 23,781 holds it [3]. Dark, saturated purple of this kind is rare in aged pigments, and these are photographs of varnished works [3]. The color is easier to find in a garden than in a museum, a point the name itself makes [3].
